summary: Veridian Health: multi-region fallback-loop triggered duplicate completions, tail-latency spike, and invoice surge
description:
Issue summary: During the 2026-03-10 morning window Veridian Health experienced a production outage pattern where requests in us-west were actively routed to fallback replicas in us-east. The fallback path entered a retry loop resulting in duplicate completions, increased tail latency, and a sharp spike in token billing for the customer.

Impact: Multiple critical customer-facing flows (patient triage summaries and medication reconciliation) returned duplicate responses and saw 95th/99th percentile tail latency increase from ~180ms to >4s. Veridian reported an unexpected 7x increase in token usage for the period and opened a billing dispute. Several requests also timed out and triggered client retries amplifying load.

Environment: Production (prod) primary region us-west, configured cross-region fallback to us-east. Customer is on enterprise plan with pinned model redwood-13b-v2. Dedicated routing policy with canary fallback enabled.

Steps to reproduce (internal repro):
1) Simulate a transient capacity drop in us-west by throttling a small group of serving-runtime pods.
2) Send steady stream of chat/generation requests with moderate context (avg 600 tokens) that exercise streaming + function calling.
3) Observe routing policy kick in and fall back to us-east.
4) Verify that client-side retry logic combined with our streaming reconnect behavior produced duplicate completions.

Relevant logs and traces:
- Correlated traces: trace_ids [trace-usw-2244, trace-use-2247] (linked in Confluence).
- Gateway error pattern: 502 then 503 followed by repeated 200s with identical completion ids.
- Billing events: billing-meter showed duplicated token_count entries for same request_ids between 2026-03-10T08:22:00Z and 2026-03-10T08:41:00Z.

Immediate customer impact: Veridian paused automated workflows, escalated to their CISO and procurement teams. They requested a corrective credit and an incident RCA within 72 hours.
investigation_notes:
Timeline:
- 2026-03-10 08:18 UTC: customer reported intermittent duplicates and spikes.
- 2026-03-10 08:22 UTC: SRE observed increased 5xxs on us-west edge and automatic failover to us-east.
- 2026-03-10 08:30 UTC: Support opened escalation and engaged infra and billing.

Hypotheses tested:
- Hypothesis A: client-side duplicate sends due to streaming disconnect. Rejected: client logs do not show duplicate send attempts before timeout.
- Hypothesis B: gateway incorrectly retried idempotent requests when fallback occurred. Confirmed: gateway retry logic triggered for streaming connections and created duplicate internal requests that reached serving-runtime.
- Hypothesis C: billing pipeline deduplication failed for cross-region proxied requests. Confirmed: dedupe key relied on request_id + region; when internal proxied request changed origin region, dedupe missed duplicates.

Root cause (short): Interaction of cross-region routing + an over-eager gateway retry path for streaming reconnects caused duplicate inference calls to be executed in the fallback region, and billing deduplication keys included region which prevented suppressing duplicate token counts.

Partial findings:
- A race in the gateway's fallback handler retried streaming attach operations without transferring the original request_id to the fallback proxy.
- Serving-runtime logged repeated completion_ids but billing ingestion assigned separate dedupe keys for us-west vs us-east.
- Autoscaling in us-east absorbed additional load but added queueing delays, increasing tail latency for affected requests.
resolution:
Immediate mitigations applied (2026-03-10):
- Disabled cross-region streaming auto-retry in the gateway for affected customer routes (hotfix rolled at 08:45 UTC).
- Short-term dedupe patch: billing ingestion logic updated to normalize request_id across proxied regions (hotfix rolled at 09:10 UTC).
- Throttled background retries on customer SDKs and advised Veridian to apply client backoff for the short window.

Permanent fixes planned and implemented:
- Gateway: ensure request_id is preserved and propagated for fallback proxy hops; added integration test; PR merged and rolled to canary 2026-03-11.
- Billing: dedupe policy changed to ignore region when request_id present; regression test added.
- Routing: implement per-customer circuit-breaker to avoid repeated cross-region failovers for 60s after first fallback.

Customer remediation:
- Issued 100% token credit for the affected window (pro-rated to their bill) and waived any accelerated support fee.
- Delivered interim status update at 2026-03-10 13:00 UTC and final RCAs and code links on 2026-03-12.

Status: All fixes deployed to prod by 2026-03-11; monitoring alerts for duplicate completions now green. Customer accepted remediation and closed escalation.
follow_up_actions:
1) Postmortem published to Confluence and shared with Veridian (link in related_confluence_pages).
2) Add integration test for cross-region request_id preservation in the infra test matrix (owner: infra-test team).
3) Add billing dedupe e2e test covering proxied requests (owner: billing).
4) Create runbook for customers on client-side backoff and recommended SDK versions.
5) Schedule internal blameless postmortem review with infra, billing, and support in next sprint.
6) Consider offering optional cross-region routing opt-out flag for enterprise customers.
